name: Light Coral
lede: Light coral is a web color, a soft pinkish red from the X11 set, defined by its hex code rather than a long history.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary lists *LightCoral* as a pinkish red, one of the 140 colors in the X11 Color Set, with the hex code #F08080 [1]. It is a web color first: the name comes from computer color lists, not from a pigment or a dye [1]. The base word [[coral]] is defined in the same book as a deep pink or reddish orange [1]. Neighbors are [[salmon]], [[light-salmon]] and [[pink]] [2]. The nearest ISCC-NBS name for the swatch is vivid pink [2]. Like every web color it is defined by a hex code, so the swatch is a screen approximation and not a dye or a paint [2]. Nothing in our books ties it to a pigment or a historical source [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Light coral is rare in painting. It appears in 5 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.02 per cent, rarer than 79 per cent of named colors, as photographed [3]. In Google Books the word peaks in the 1930s [4].
